title: Chamber Welcomes 14 New Members in First Half of 2026
author: Chamber Staff
excerpt: From a new coffee roaster to a fourth-generation trailer dealer, meet the businesses that joined the Greater Haralson Chamber this spring.
body:
The Greater Haralson Chamber is proud to welcome 14 new member businesses in the first half of 2026, bringing total membership past the 700 mark for the first time in the organization's history.

New members span every corner of the county — new storefronts in downtown Bremen and Tallapoosa, two home-based businesses making the leap to their first commercial space, and several long-standing county businesses joining the chamber for the first time.

"Crossing 700 members says something simple: businesses here believe we're stronger together," said chamber president Lena Morrow. "Every one of these 14 has a story, and our job is to make sure the rest of the county hears it."

Each new member receives a ribbon cutting, a feature across the chamber's social channels, and a listing in the online member directory. If you know a business that ought to be part of the chamber, send them to our Become a Member page — or better yet, bring them to the next luncheon as your guest.

title: Member Spotlight: 74 Years of Haralson Hardware & Supply
author: Chamber Staff
excerpt: Three generations, one Main Street address, and a checker table that has outlasted every big-box scare. How Buchanan's hardware store keeps winning.
body:
When Troy Abernathy's grandfather opened Haralson Hardware & Supply in 1952, Main Street in Buchanan had two other hardware stores. Both are long gone. Haralson Hardware is still here — same address, same family, and by Troy's count, some of the same customers' families four generations deep.

"People ask how we compete with the big boxes," Troy says, restocking a bin of carriage bolts sold by the each, not the box of fifty. "We don't compete with them. We do the things they can't. You come in with a broken part, somebody here has fixed one before. You need three feet of chain, we cut you three feet of chain."

The store's famous front-counter checker table — original to 1952 — still hosts a standing game most mornings. Troy's daughter Kate, the third generation, has added online ordering for farm deliveries and a small-engine repair bench that stays booked two weeks out.

Asked what the chamber means to a business that predates it joining by a decade, Troy doesn't hesitate: "When the bypass talk had everybody scared in the nineties, it was the chamber that got the merchants in one room. You can't put a price on having somebody whose whole job is pulling for the county."

Haralson Hardware & Supply is open Monday through Saturday at 355 Main Street in Buchanan.

title: Fall Festival Food Truck Spots Open — Craft Booths Sold Out in Record Time
author: Chamber Staff
excerpt: The September 19 Fall Festival on the Square sold out its 100 craft vendor booths in eleven days. A handful of food truck spots remain.
body:
Downtown Tallapoosa's Fall Festival on the Square, set for Saturday, September 19, has sold out all 100 craft vendor booths — in eleven days, a record for the event's history.

A limited number of food truck and food vendor spots remain available. Priority goes to chamber members and Haralson County-based operators; the vendor fee is $125 and includes power hookup and two parking passes. Contact the chamber office to apply.

This year's festival adds a second music stage on Lyon Street and expands the kids' zone with a climbing wall and petting zoo from Little River Farms. The classic car cruise-in returns to its usual stretch of Head Avenue, and the chamber's funnel cake booth — staffed, as tradition demands, by the board of directors in aprons — benefits the Haralson Youth Sports Foundation.

Last year's festival drew an estimated 6,000 visitors to downtown Tallapoosa. Merchants reported their strongest single-day sales of the fall. "The festival is exactly what this chamber exists to do," said events chair Danielle Sikes. "Fill the square, and the businesses around it win."

title: Member Spotlight: Sweetwater Bakery Turns a Depot Street Storefront Into a Destination
author: Chamber Staff
excerpt: Marisol Vega opened Sweetwater Bakery in Waco with a mixer, a credit card, and a cinnamon roll recipe. Five years later, Saturday mornings have a line.
body:
Waco doesn't have a stoplight, but on Saturday mornings it has a line. It forms outside Sweetwater Bakery on Depot Street around 6:45, fifteen minutes before Marisol Vega unlocks the door, and it doesn't let up until the cinnamon rolls are gone — usually by ten.

Vega opened the bakery in 2019 in a storefront that had sat empty for six years. "Everyone told me to open in Bremen or Carrollton, somewhere with traffic," she says. "But rent here let me start without drowning, and honestly? Being the reason people drive to Waco — I liked that idea."

Custom cakes are now the engine of the business: weddings across west Georgia, graduation season so busy she caps orders in April, and a growing line of quinceañera cakes that draw families from as far as Douglasville. She hired her first full-time employee last year and a second this spring — one of them a Haralson County High grad she met through the school's work-based learning program.

Vega joined the chamber the month she opened, and credits her first wedding cake booking to a bride who found her in the member directory. "I was brand new. Nobody knew me. Being on that list made me real."

Sweetwater Bakery is open Wednesday through Saturday, 7am to 2pm — but for the cinnamon rolls, you know when to show up.
